description: The chart illustrates the distribution of datasets by the number of data sources over time, comparing those collected from a single source to those collected from multiple sources. The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, with the categories listed in chronological order. The vertical axis is labeled "Number of datasets" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 100, with tick labels at intervals of 20. The chart features grouped bars, with each group representing a year and containing two bars: a blue bar representing datasets collected from a single source ("1") and an orange bar representing datasets collected from two or more sources ("2+"). The blue bars generally increase in height over time, with values ranging from 1 in 2013 to 108 in 2021, while the orange bars remain relatively low until 2018, after which they also increase, with values ranging from 1 in 2012 to 44 in 2020. The bars are not sorted in a specific order within each group, and there is no visual emphasis on particular bars. The chart provides a clear visual representation of the shift in data collection practices over time, with a notable increase in datasets collected from multiple sources around 2018.
